questions.stem: What are the three subatomic particles found in an atom?

options.text: Protons, neutrons, and ions
Neutrons, electrons, and positrons
Protons, neutrons, and electrons
Protons, photons, and electrons

questions.explanation: An atom contains protons (positive charge, in the nucleus), neutrons (no charge, in the nucleus), and electrons (negative charge, orbiting in shells around the nucleus).

questions.stem: What does the atomic number of an element tell you?

options.text: The number of neutrons in the nucleus
The total number of protons and neutrons
The number of electron shells
The number of protons in the nucleus

questions.explanation: The atomic number (Z) is the number of protons in the nucleus. It defines which element the atom is. In a neutral atom, it also equals the number of electrons.

questions.stem: What is the approximate diameter of an atom?

options.text: 10 to the power of minus 5 metres
10 to the power of minus 2 metres
10 to the power of minus 10 metres
10 to the power of minus 15 metres

questions.explanation: An atom has a diameter of approximately 10 to the power of minus 10 metres (0.1 nanometres). The nucleus is much smaller, about 10 to the power of minus 15 metres.

options.text: Atoms of the same element with different numbers of electrons
Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons
Atoms of different elements with the same mass number
Atoms of the same element with different numbers of protons

questions.explanation: Isotopes are atoms of the same element (same number of protons) but with different numbers of neutrons, giving them different mass numbers. They have identical chemical properties.

questions.stem: An atom has 6 protons and 8 neutrons. What is its mass number?
questions.explanation: The mass number (A) equals the total number of protons plus neutrons in the nucleus. So A = 6 + 8 = 14. This is carbon-14, an isotope of carbon.

questions.stem: What did Rutherford's alpha particle scattering experiment prove about the atom?

options.text: That atoms contain electrons
That atoms are solid spheres of positive charge
That neutrons exist inside the nucleus
That most of the atom is empty space with a small, dense, positively charged nucleus

questions.explanation: Most alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil (showing the atom is mostly empty space), while a few were deflected at large angles or bounced back (showing a small, dense, positively charged nucleus).

questions.stem: Which subatomic particle has a relative charge of minus 1?

options.text: Alpha particle
Electron
Proton
Neutron

questions.explanation: The electron has a relative charge of minus 1. The proton has a relative charge of plus 1, and the neutron has zero charge.
